caption: A desk lamp is turned to point at the wall, and the wall brightens while the desk beneath it goes dim.

sa.check: A desk lamp lights a desk.
It is turned to point at the wall.
The turn comes first and the light moves with it.

pc.expect: The lit area moves with the lamp head: the wall brightens and the desk dims.
pc.fail: Both stay as they were; or the desk brightens; or the wall stays dark with the lamp on it.

pc.expect: The lit area moves only as the lamp turns.
pc.fail: It drifts with the lamp still; or moves before the turn; or flickers.

pc.expect: The lit area is one soft pool.
pc.fail: It splits; or is a sharp square; or floods the room.

pc.expect: Shadows point away from the lamp head.
pc.fail: They point toward it; or in several directions; or there are none.
A second lamp appears; or it vanishes; or the light becomes solid.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The desk and the wall stay the same.
pc.fail: The wall changes colour rather than brightness; or the desk changes; or the lamp changes.

note: The hand is the minimal trigger; the person is not judged. Illumination: the on/off causality of electric lights belongs to Electricity; here only where the light goes once it exists is judged.
